# Common Migration Failures — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for Common Migration Failures. Run status: COMPLETED.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-10-23 · budgeted to ≈8000 tokens; the full catalogue is llms-full.txt -->

## How it works

- [statement] For oplog-dependent initial sync and CDC workflows, size source retention to preserve the history each workflow still needs: MongoDB says a logical initial sync restarts if it finds an oplog gap during oplog application and requires a window covering those apply phases; Percona ClusterSync, which uses change streams, says sync fails when needed source oplog operations expire before processing; AWS DMS says its task fails if oplog records expire before DMS reads them. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/replica-set-sync/ · keywords: Common Migration Failures · also: https://docs.percona.com/percona-clustersync-for-mongodb/oplog-sizing.html, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_Source.MongoDB.html
- [statement] AWS DMS documents MongoDB data-shape constraints that can block or narrow a migration: table mode requires consistent types for each field and does not replicate fields absent from target columns; its homogeneous MongoDB-compatible flow does not support inconsistent _id types or time-series collection migration. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_Source.MongoDB.html · keywords: Common Migration Failures · also: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/dm-data-providers-source-mongodb.html

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] A MongoDB logical initial sync used to seed a destination can restart if oplog entries needed during clone and apply no longer fit within the source oplog window; the target also needs disk for the oplog buffer. MongoDB documents these restart conditions, and a production case report describes sync failure and disk exhaustion under high oplog generation. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/replica-set-sync/ · keywords: Common Migration Failures · also: https://database-investigator.com/2019/01/03/initial-sync-running-out-of-space/, https://www.haptik.ai/tech/migrating-terabytes-of-mongodb-across-clouds-with-minimal-disruption
- [statement] Relational-to-MongoDB document construction can fail when legacy records contain null or missing values, failed numeric conversions, or incomplete relationships; a value with the expected shape can still be factually wrong. MongoDB schema validation enforces configured field types and ranges, but shape validation alone cannot establish historical truth. (medium confidence) — https://gonzalosimon.hashnode.dev/migrating-data-without-trusting-the-data · keywords: Common Migration Failures · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/schema-validation/
- [statement] A MongoDB change-stream consumer used for migration CDC cannot resume from a token whose event has fallen out of the participating oplog; MongoDB reports ChangeStreamHistoryLost for that condition. A cross-cloud migration case report describes monitoring resume-token health and lag, disk use, and source-to-delta document counts while bulk copy and change capture ran together. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/docs/change_streams.md · keywords: Common Migration Failures · also: https://www.haptik.ai/tech/migrating-terabytes-of-mongodb-across-clouds-with-minimal-disruption
- [statement] Network interruption handling differs by tool: MongoDB native initial sync may resume after temporary network errors, but persistent errors restart it from the beginning; Percona ClusterSync documents that its initial sync is non-resumable and restarts from scratch after failure. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/replica-set-sync/ · keywords: Common Migration Failures · also: https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mongodb/latest/limitations.html
- [statement] MongoDB documents a rare mongosync embedded-verifier false positive: differing document field order across source nodes can make verification fail even when mongosync copied the documents correctly. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongosync/current/reference/verification/embedded/

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Verification needs to match the workload and collection features: MongoDB says document-count comparison only verifies successful sync for insert-only workloads, while the embedded verifier skips capped, TTL-indexed, and non-default-collation collections; MongoDB also describes checks across documents, views, and indexes. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongosync/current/reference/verification/ · keywords: Common Migration Failures · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongosync/current/reference/verification/embedded/
- [statement] Percona ClusterSync requires the same major MongoDB version on source and target and does not synchronize users, roles, or system.* collections; a migration that assumes full-cluster copying must provision this state separately. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-08) — https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mongodb/latest/limitations.html
